Quote not verbatim in evidence (Evidence includes the opening and closing lines but not the clause about ‘AI companions’ and ‘recovery’ (snippet 5).): Each month that passes makes physical reality feel more foreign, AI companions more appealing, and recovery more distant

No evidence snippet or report excerpt was provided that discusses engagement strategy or the idea that identity formation sits upstream of purchase behaviour.: This audience is economically material, but engagement must account for identity formation that sits upstream of purchase behavior and brand affinity.

No explicit evidence was supplied that tells leaders what they 'should expect'; the statement is an inference rather than a cited report finding.: Leaders should expect persistent tension between online self-presentation and offline competence.

While evidence supports culture-creation decline and short-lived AI cycles, no snippet addresses the claimed reduction of “durable cultural scaffolding for maturation.”: Culture creation is faltering, with identity fragmentation and short-lived AI content cycles, which reduces durable cultural scaffolding for maturation.

No evidence snippet discusses strategic risks of ‘leaning further into algorithmic dependency.’: Strategies that lean further into algorithmic dependency risk amplifying the very dynamics that hold this cohort back.

Evidence backs the phrase “sweat, not screens” and rising urgency, but no snippet supports the need to rebuild “social fluency.”: Shift resources toward embodied, offline experiences to rebuild competence and social fluency, as the report states the path back to culture starts with “sweat, not screens,” and urgency increases eac

The evidence shows success is redefined around digital metrics, but no excerpt recommends ‘rebalancing’ those definitions.: Rebalance success definitions away from “success defined by digital metrics” toward real-world participation and capability-building outcomes.

No evidence snippet makes this operational recommendation or cites algorithmic environments that ‘entrench safety, predictability, and passive consumption.’: Operate with a dual-lens that recognizes stable contradictions at the core of Gen Q identities while reducing reliance on algorithmic environments that entrench safety, predictability, and passive con
This prescriptive claim lacks direct support in the supplied evidence.: Growth with Gen Q will not be won by more screen time.
No evidence snippet offers this specific strategic instruction.: Rebalance from digital-only engagement to embodied experiences.
The supplied evidence does not contain this design recommendation.: Design programs, events, and services that build physical-world competence and connection.

Although the report mentions mutations becoming super-powers, no snippet recommends specific ‘pathways’ to translate fluency into capability.: Offer pathways that translate online fluency into real-world capability, converting “mutations” into strengths.
No evidence excerpt provides guidance on measurement practices.: Measure beyond vanity metrics.
No snippet offers this prescriptive direction to builders or brands.: Build for creation, not just consumption.
No evidence snippet supplies this product-design recommendation.: Design for contradiction.

The evidence describes platform-induced harms and a trust crisis but does not instruct brands to ‘acknowledge’ them in communications.: Acknowledge platform-induced harms and the trust crisis in your experiences and communications.
